function f() {}

// cycPos has nine ifs: cyclomatic 1 + 9 = 10.
function cycPos(x) {
  if (x.a) { f(); }
  if (x.b) { f(); }
  if (x.c) { f(); }
  if (x.d) { f(); }
  if (x.a) { f(); }
  if (x.b) { f(); }
  if (x.c) { f(); }
  if (x.d) { f(); }
  if (x.a) { f(); }
}

// cycNeg has eight ifs: cyclomatic 9.
function cycNeg(x) {
  if (x.a) { f(); }
  if (x.b) { f(); }
  if (x.c) { f(); }
  if (x.d) { f(); }
  if (x.a) { f(); }
  if (x.b) { f(); }
  if (x.c) { f(); }
  if (x.d) { f(); }
}

// nestPos nests four ifs: depth 4, one bump, cyclomatic 5.
function nestPos(x) {
  if (x.a) {
    if (x.b) {
      if (x.c) {
        if (x.d) {
          f();
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

// nestNeg nests three ifs: depth 3, one bump, cyclomatic 4.
function nestNeg(x) {
  if (x.a) {
    if (x.b) {
      if (x.c) {
        f();
      }
    }
  }
}

// bumpsPos has two separate top-level blocks that reach depth 2.
function bumpsPos(x) {
  if (x.a) {
    if (x.b) {
      f();
    }
  }
  f();
  if (x.c) {
    if (x.d) {
      f();
    }
  }
}

// bumpsNeg has one nested block and one flat if.
function bumpsNeg(x) {
  if (x.a) {
    if (x.b) {
      f();
    }
  }
  if (x.c) {
    f();
  }
}

// boolPos has three boolean operators in one condition.
function boolPos(x) {
  if (x.a && x.b && x.c || x.d) {
    f();
  }
}

// boolNeg has two boolean operators in one condition.
function boolNeg(x) {
  if (x.a && x.b || x.c) {
    f();
  }
}

// argsPos has five parameters.
function argsPos(a, b, c, d, e) {}

// argsNeg has four parameters.
function argsNeg(a, b, c, d) {}

// primPos would be primitive obsession in TypeScript; JavaScript declares no
// types, so the smell is unsupported and never reported.
function primPos(a, b, c, d) {}

// primNeg: four parameters.
function primNeg(a, b, c, d) {}

// primFew: three parameters.
function primFew(a, b, c) {}

// params: plain, default-valued and rest parameters each count once.
function params(a, b = 2, ...rest) {}

// constructs uses every ECMAScript decision point once; default is not one.
function constructs(a, xs, x) {
  if (x.a && x.b || x.c) {
    a++;
  } else if (x.d) {
    a--;
  }
  for (let i = 0; i < a; i++) {}
  for (const e of xs) {}
  for (const k in x) {}
  while (a > 100) { a--; }
  do { a++; } while (a < 3);
  switch (a) {
    case 1:
    case 2:
      break;
    default:
      break;
  }
  try { f(); } catch (e) { f(); }
  const t = x.a ? 1 : 2;
  const u = x.b ?? x.c;
  a ||= 1;
  a &&= 2;
  a ??= 3;
  return a;
}

// elseIf is a chain on one level.
function elseIf(x) {
  if (x.a) {
    f();
  } else if (x.b) {
    f();
  } else if (x.c) {
    f();
  } else {
    f();
  }
}

const arrow = (y) => {
  if (y.a) { f(); }
};

class Service {
  run(x) {
    if (x.a) { f(); }
  }

  field = (x) => {
    if (x.b) { f(); }
  };
}

// closures: the callbacks are anonymous and count toward the function; run is
// a named closure and a unit of its own; inner is a nested function.
function closures(x, items) {
  const run = () => {
    if (x.a) { f(); }
  };
  items.forEach((item) => {
    if (item.b) { f(); }
  });
  items.map(function (item) {
    for (const k in item) { f(); }
    return item;
  });
  function inner() {
    if (x.c) { f(); }
  }
}

// A single unparenthesised arrow parameter counts once.
const single = x => x.a ? 1 : 2;

export default function () {
  if (single(1)) { f(); }
}

const holder = {
  handler: function (e) { if (e) { f(); } },
  method(e) { if (e) { f(); } },
};

exports.shared = function (e) { if (e) { f(); } };
